Akira Kurosawa season, Strathbungo Film Society, February and March 2025. Six films, Sundays at 2pm because "Seven Samurai" is 207 minutes and nobody survives that on a weeknight. The shot-by-shot framing notes are in Japanese, in [[黒澤明の構図]]; this one is the season, the films and the arguments.

## Why Kurosawa

Because every western, every heist film and half of "Star Wars" borrowed from him and the club should see the originals on something bigger than a laptop. Also because I saw "Yojimbo" at the GFT in 1997 and haven't been right since.

## The season

### 2 February: "Rashomon" (1950)

Four versions of one killing in a forest. Won the Golden Lion at Venice in 1951. Shot the sun directly through the leaves, which was supposedly bad luck at the time. 33 people. The discussion after ran 50 minutes, longest we've ever had. Ishbel says the woodcutter is lying too. She's right.

### 9 February: "Ikiru" (1952)

Takashi Shimura as the dying civil servant, singing "Gondola no Uta" on the swing in the snow. Two men in the back row cried. The second half is the wake, told in flashback by the people who knew him, structure worth stealing, see [[Screenwriting structure]].

### 16 February: "Seven Samurai" (1954)

207 minutes plus the intermission. Ran it with a 15-minute tea break, shortbread from Ishbel's mum. Final battle in the mud and rain: Kurosawa added ink to the rain water so it would show up on black-and-white stock. 29 started, 27 finished.

### 2 March: "Yojimbo" (1961)

Toshiro Mifune shrugging his shoulders. The dog with the hand in its mouth. Masaru Sato's score sounds like a jazz band fell down the stairs, in a good way. Leone remade it as "A Fistful of Dollars" (1964) without asking.

### 16 March: "High and Low" (1963)

Kidnap thriller. First hour all in one hilltop living room, then the city. The pink smoke from the chimney in a black-and-white film, one colour shot. 36 people, best attendance of the season.

### 30 March: "Ran" (1985)

King Lear with three sons. Colour, 162 minutes, Emi Wada's costumes won the Oscar. Tatsuya Nakadai's make-up is a Noh mask. The castle burning was a real castle set built on the slopes of Mount Fuji, and burned once, no second take.

## Mifune

16 films together between 1948 and 1965, then they fell out over "Red Beard" and never worked together again. Nobody quite knows why. I have theories, none useful.

## Technique, briefly

Multiple cameras running at once on long lenses, so actors didn't know which one was on them. Wipes between scenes (Lucas took those). Weather as mood: rain, wind, heat haze in "Stray Dog" (1949). The detail is in the Japanese note.

## Practical

- Prints: DCPs from the BFI for "Ran" and "Seven Samurai", Blu-rays from the Criterion boxset for the rest. Licence ref FB-61407.
- Subtitles: the Criterion ones are better than the old BFI ones for "Yojimbo".
- Ishbel went to [[Kyoto]] in April and sent a photo from the site of the Daiei studio where "Rashomon" was shot. It's a car park now.

## Takings

Six screenings, 181 tickets at £4, £724. Licences £510 total ("Seven Samurai" alone £120). Small profit. Next director season: Agnès Varda, autumn 2025.
